description: Adobe AVX2 Patch changes the installer requirements of Adobe products, replacing the AVX2 check with AVX. This lets users install recent Adobe software on older processors that do not support the AVX2 instruction set.

A separate 64‑bit DXVK rendering process (RTX Remix Bridge) moves renderer allocations outside the game's 32‑bit address space, helping with memory usage.

name: GunWall
summary: A free, open‑source application firewall for Windows that blocks programs from accessing the internet until you allow them.
description: GunWall monitors outgoing network connections and lets you decide which applications are allowed to connect. When a program tries to reach the internet for the first time, GunWall shows a prompt with details about the program and its destination, letting you create a rule to allow or block it. GunWall works with the Windows Filtering Platform, the same kernel layer used by Windows Firewall, so it does not require a separate proxy or driver. You can create per‑application rules, custom address/port rules, block traffic by country or network operator, and use rule profiles for different locations. An integrated network scanner identifies devices on your local network, and an optional local DNS resolver with DNS‑over‑HTTPS can block trackers and ads using customizable blocklists. All changes that reduce protection require administrator approval, and turning GunWall off or uninstalling it restores the default Windows network behavior.

name: keep-sorted
summary: A language‑agnostic formatter that sorts lines between two markers in a file.
description: keep-sorted is a small command‑line utility that automatically orders lines of code or data that are enclosed by special marker comments. It works with many programming languages and file types without needing language‑specific knowledge.

The tool looks for comment markers such as // keep-sorted start and // keep-sorted end (or similar markers in other languages). All lines between the markers are treated as a block and are sorted alphabetically. This helps keep import lists, module declarations, array initializers, and other ordered sections tidy and consistent. keep-sorted can handle simple line continuations, more complex blocks with balanced symbols, and custom prefix grouping. It can be run directly on files or used in a pre‑commit hook to enforce sorting automatically.

description: WristKey lets you lock your PC automatically when you walk away and unlock it instantly when you return, using the proximity of your Apple Watch. It works in the background and keeps your credentials encrypted.

WristKey replaces Windows’ built‑in Dynamic Lock with a true proximity solution based on Apple’s Continuity protocol. The app continuously monitors BLE advertisements from your Apple Watch. When the watch is out of range or removed from your wrist, the PC is locked. The program runs as a credential provider and shows a real‑time status panel with RSSI tracking and validation information. It is designed for users who want a macOS‑like auto‑unlock experience on Windows without relying on the slower Dynamic Lock feature.

name: XR Gate
summary: An open‑source runtime that lets Windows run VR/AR headsets and controllers that lack native support, providing 6DoF tracking, hand tracking and body tracking for SteamVR and OpenXR applications.
description: XR Gate is a free, open‑source software package that acts as a bridge between limited or unsupported XR hardware and Windows VR platforms. It captures camera and IMU data, processes it, and presents it to SteamVR, OpenXR or other VR applications as if the hardware were natively supported. The project is aimed at users who want to use devices such as XREAL Ultra glasses, Leap Motion cameras or custom trackers for VR gaming and research without needing proprietary drivers.

The program works by running a capture service that reads stereo camera images and optional IMU data, then streams the information to a client library. The client normalises the data, predicts movement, and provides virtual controller input. Supported features include:

* Full 6DoF head tracking using stereo cameras and optional IMU integration. * Image‑based hand tracking via the Mercury/ONNX backend. * Optional body‑tracking using the FRAME backend. * Compatibility with a range of controllers, including Samsung Gear VR and generic Bluetooth gamepads. * Integration with SteamVR/OpenVR and OpenXR runtimes, allowing existing VR games to work. * Stereo video streaming and optional video overlay for mixed‑reality experiments. * Real‑time depth grid and spatial mesh output for research purposes.

The Windows version is packaged as a portable ZIP that runs under WSL2 with USB‑IP support, providing the necessary driver bridge for USB‑connected devices. No vendor‑specific SDKs are required, and the system can be used with a variety of headsets and tracking setups.
Features are implemented in C++ for low‑latency capture and in Python for flexible SDK access, making the stack both performant and extensible.
The project is licensed under the MIT license and is maintained on GitHub.
